models.limits: Atomic store-level ownership of EC2-owned VPCs, subnets and launch records beside stack-owned networks and instance claims, authorization order, the single-writer client token, dependent protection and the record quota only. One region: the per-region token scope and the database-wide quota are not distinguished. A token replay and a token mismatch are both a refused write: which record is returned and the parameter hash are not modeled. Stack deletion is one step that always succeeds. Native Go tests, the boto3 lifecycle, the browser end-to-end flow and the Scalar Send flow establish those implementation properties.

New native launch-record store: RunInstances inserts one record below an EC2-owned subnet in one transaction, replays or refuses a repeated client token without writing, enforces the record bound and reads the row back; TerminateInstances removes exactly one EC2-owned record and refuses a stack's instance. Rows that disagree with their key columns, subnet or a stack claim fail closed. No guest is started and no runtime state is stored.
